questions.q: Which DMF returns direct physical fragmentation statistics for indexes?
options: sys.dm_exec_requests
sys.dm_os_wait_stats
sys.dm_db_index_physical_stats
sys.dm_db_file_space_usage
questions.explain: It's the function that takes database/object/index/partition/scan-mode arguments and returns per-index fragmentation and page counts.

questions.q: Why is the 'LIMITED' scan mode preferred over 'DETAILED' for routine production checks?
options: It is the only mode that returns avg_fragmentation_in_percent
It only reads parent-level pages, making it much cheaper to run against a live production database
'LIMITED' mode automatically rebuilds any fragmented index it finds
'DETAILED' mode is deprecated and no longer supported
questions.explain: 'LIMITED' is a lightweight scan; 'DETAILED' reads every page and is far more expensive to run.

questions.q: Per Microsoft's documented guidance, what's the recommended action for an index between 10% and 30% fragmented?
options: ALTER INDEX ... REORGANIZE
ALTER INDEX ... REBUILD
No action is ever recommended below 30%
DROP and recreate the index manually
questions.explain: 10%-30% is the documented range for REORGANIZE; over 30% is when REBUILD is recommended instead.

questions.q: Why does page_count matter alongside avg_fragmentation_in_percent when deciding whether to act on fragmentation?
options: page_count determines whether REORGANIZE is even a valid operation on that index
SQL Server refuses to rebuild any index with fewer than 1,000 pages
A small index with few pages sees little real I/O impact from fragmentation, even at a high percentage
page_count has no real bearing on the decision at all
questions.explain: A tiny index fits in a handful of extents and is often already cached — fragmentation there barely changes access patterns.

questions.q: What is the key operational difference between REORGANIZE and REBUILD?
options: There is no meaningful difference between the two operations
REORGANIZE permanently deletes the index; REBUILD only updates statistics
REORGANIZE is always online and incremental; REBUILD recreates the index in one operation and locks more heavily unless run with ONLINE = ON
REBUILD is always faster and lower-impact than REORGANIZE regardless of edition
questions.explain: REORGANIZE defragments in small steps with minimal locking; REBUILD is more thorough but more resource-intensive.
